messages.text:
I haven't replied in the chat. Following the defective-verdict rule, I recorded the BS-4 as defective and the chat went back to Sarah, who answers this customer's "hello?".

**The fault:** Two of the four chips do no work. The log shows `nonce distribution: 1053/1026/0/0` after more than an hour, along with repeated `invalid asic 4 / 6` errors. That's why the pool sees about 9.7 TH/s while the miner shows 19. It's the same after several restarts, including switching off at the wall, and temperatures and fans are normal. In the RMA triage notes, JD lists "only some chips hashing from the first plug-in" as a broken voltage regulator (TPS), which is a board fault, so I didn't wait for him to answer.

**What JD or Georges should know before approving:**
- **No video or serial photo.** The only evidence is the log text the customer typed into the chat.
- **Order Shop···· is my best guess.** It's the newer of their two orders and they said they "just got" the unit, but I didn't look it up to check which order the BS-4 came on.
- **The customer never asked for a return.** They asked for an update, after being flagged to JD twice with no reply. The approval may come as news to them.
- **Firmware 1.3 is unconfirmed.** BitFortun doesn't publish BS-4 firmware, so I couldn't check whether 1.3 is the latest. If JD knows of a newer version, it's worth one flash before the unit comes back.

The team is online now (Monday 4:31 PM ET).
